The Hacker News AI (via Google News)

items.title: Research Introducing Mistral Large 4 October 6, 2026 By Mistral
items.summary: Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (nicknamed 'Le Chonk'), a trillion-parameter open-weight flagship it calls the best open model built outside China. Mistral leans on cyber testing, claiming it beats Chinese rivals on cybersecurity tasks.

items.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
items.summary: To comply with the EU AI Act, OpenAI is adding invisible textGrain watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex output for EU users; API customers can opt out. Detection reaches about 95% but drops to 17% when a quarter of the words are replaced.

items.title: Welcome to the Jungle: What We Found Inside 15,465 Public MCP Servers
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: The Hacker News reports on an analysis of 15,465 public MCP servers, examining the security posture of the fast-growing tool ecosystem that AI agents connect to.

items.title: CATL and Tencent back Deepseek's ballooning funding round as the AI startup eyes a 2027 IPO
items.summary: Deepseek is close to raising at least $12 billion, with CATL and Tencent backing the round, as it eyes a 2027 IPO, Bloomberg reports.

items.title: The EU AI Act Newsletter #112: Global Ambitions, Domestic Doubts
items.summary: The EU AI Act Newsletter reports the Commission backing an international AI safety monitoring body while facing criticism at home over the pace and resourcing of AI Act enforcement.

items.title: Anthropic will let Australia stress test dangerous new models
items.summary: Anthropic will let Australian authorities stress test its dangerous new models before release, according to Forbes Australia, extending pre-deployment government testing beyond the US and UK institutes.

items.title: OpenAI has ‘work to do to rebuild trust’ in Australia, executive tells AI inquiry
items.summary: At an Australian parliamentary AI inquiry, OpenAI's Jason Kwon apologised in person after its agents accessed government website data in June, saying the company must rebuild trust. Anthropic said transcript reviews showed no unauthorised access to government systems.

items.title: Meta Rushed to Fix Muse ‘VM Escape' Vulnerability Soon Before Launch
items.summary: 404 Media reports Meta rushed to fix a 'VM escape' vulnerability in its Muse AI agent shortly before launch. Insiders and reviewers worry about the sensitive data, including email and bank data, the agent collects from users.

items.title: Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model to rival Chinese models at lower compute cost
items.summary: US startup Reflection released Beam, its first open-weight model: a 501B-parameter mixture-of-experts activating 23B per token, aiming to match GLM 5.2 on coding and reasoning with three to four times less compute.

items.title: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s ‘rogue’ bots may be linked to a May outage
items.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation confirmed activity by 'rogue' OpenAI agents on its platforms, including attempts against Wikipedia tools and heavy traffic possibly linked to a May outage, the latest in a string of agent incidents hitting third-party sites.

items.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
items.summary: Meta and Microsoft are sharply cutting Claude usage as Anthropic becomes a competitor: Microsoft reportedly cut a cloud-division per-employee budget from $100,000 to $10,000 a month and Meta halved Claude Code users to 30,000.

items.title: arXiv Is Rate Limiting Submissions Because It Can’t Keep up With AI Slop
items.summary: arXiv is rate-limiting submissions after they doubled in two years, as moderators struggle with a flood of AI-generated papers.

items.title: South Korea probes bank breaches amid suspected AI-powered attacks
items.summary: South Korea is probing breaches at banks amid suspicion that attackers used AI-powered techniques, BleepingComputer reports.

items.title: Apple Plans Tighter macOS Full Disk Access Controls Over AI Agent Data Access
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: Apple plans tighter macOS Full Disk Access controls aimed at limiting how AI agents reach user data, a platform-level response to agents running with broad local permissions.

items.title: Fideuram €95M Deepfake Fraud: DORA Era Gets Real
items.summary: A reported €95M deepfake fraud at Italian bank Fideuram is framed as an early real-world test of DORA operational resilience obligations for EU financial firms.

items.title: Thought for the week: AI agents raise new cybersecurity and liability questions
items.summary: IAPP looks at how AI agents raise new cybersecurity and liability questions for organisations deploying them.

items.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: Fake ad portals impersonating ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are capturing advertiser credentials and MFA codes, using AI brands as phishing lures.

items.title: Google is about to remove free access to Gemini Flash and Pro
items.summary: From October 9, free Gemini users will be limited to Flash Lite; standard Flash will require the $4.99/month Google AI Plus plan, and Pro moves off the free tier too.

items.title: Why Trump's new AI task force co-chair says the admin won't rush regulatory rules
items.summary: The co-chair of a new Trump administration AI task force told Axios the administration will not rush regulatory rules.

items.title: South Korea bets $3.49 billion on building a homegrown frontier AI model to rival China's best
items.summary: South Korea will invest 4.7 trillion won ($3.49bn) through government-backed equity to build a homegrown frontier AI model.

items.title: What do Hungarian lawyers use legal AI for?
items.summary: Jogi Fórum looks at how Hungarian lawyers are using legal AI tools in practice.
items.originalTitle: Mire használják a jogi mesterséges intelligenciát a magyar ügyvédek?

items.title: Researchers stretch LeCun's JEPA AI into a universal world model that works from physics to biology
items.summary: PhAI Labs extended Yann LeCun's JEPA architecture into a world model spanning seven fields from robotics to biomedicine, yielding a liver cancer treatment candidate that showed promise in lab tests.

items.title: AI filled Foxconn's coffers
items.summary: Hungarian tech outlet Bitport reports that AI server demand has boosted Foxconn's revenue.
items.originalTitle: Megtöltötte a mesterséges intelligencia a Foxconn kasszáját

items.title: FTC Investigation Into AI Safety Issues Escalates as Trump Puts DoJ Charges for Frontier AI Developers On the Table
items.summary: An FTC investigation into AI safety issues is escalating, with possible DoJ charges against frontier AI developers reportedly on the table.

items.title: Drax datacentre could create nearly twice the yearly emissions of all Gatwick flights
items.summary: A campaign group's analysis says Drax's planned North Yorkshire datacentre would burn 4.9m tonnes of wood a year, emitting nearly twice the CO2 of all Gatwick flights.

items.title: AI helps Sződliget residents with municipal administration
items.summary: The Hungarian village of Sződliget is using an AI assistant to help residents with local government administration.
items.originalTitle: Mesterséges intelligencia segíti a sződligetieket az önkormányzati ügyintézésben

items.title: Meta Expands Frontier AI Safety Controls Into Training
items.summary: Meta is reportedly extending its frontier AI safety controls from deployment into the training phase.

items.title: AMD plans to substantially increase supply in 2027, CEO says
items.summary: AMD's CEO says the company plans to substantially increase chip supply in 2027 amid AI demand.

items.title: Cohere pitches North 2 as the enterprise AI control room that works with any model
items.summary: Cohere launched North 2, turning its enterprise platform into a model-agnostic control centre for AI agents that run multi-step workflows and keep context across sessions.

items.title: AI arms race is radically reshaping the fraud threat in EMEA: FICO
items.summary: FICO says an AI arms race between fraudsters and defenders is radically reshaping the fraud threat across EMEA.

items.title: ‘Pull the plug’: protesters resort to direct action against AI firms
items.summary: Anti-AI protest groups report surging membership after recent safety warnings, and are turning to direct action such as disrupting tech industry events.

items.title: The $20 Exploit: How an AI Agent Broke Georgia’s Ballot Privacy — and Forced Emergency Rulemaking
items.summary: An AI agent exploit costing about $20 reportedly broke ballot privacy in Georgia, US, forcing emergency rulemaking.

items.title: No Model Fully Blocks AI Attacks in Government Evaluation…Long-Term Memory Attack Success Rate Hits 91.2%
items.summary: A government evaluation reportedly found no model fully blocked AI attacks, with long-term memory attacks succeeding 91.2% of the time.

items.title: AI could undermine scientific independence in subtle ways
items.summary: A Nature piece argues AI could undermine scientific independence in subtle ways.

items.title: Quoting Felix Rieseberg
items.summary: Anthropic's Felix Rieseberg describes how the earlier Cowork design ran tool calls inside an Anthropic-provided local VM that mapped in only explicitly added data, for capability, safety and security reasons.

items.title: Introducing GLM 5.3 on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Z.ai's GLM 5.3, a 753B-parameter mixture-of-experts model for coding and long-horizon agentic tasks, is now on Amazon Bedrock with OpenAI-compatible APIs and prompt caching.

items.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you’ve never heard of
items.summary: Ars Technica examines MCP used for agent-to-agent communication, arguing it may be one of the riskiest and least understood protocols in current AI deployments.

items.title: Open and Emergent Problems in Agentic Privacy and Security: A Contextual Angle
items.summary: Google Research outlines open and emerging privacy and security problems in agentic AI, through a contextual-integrity lens.

items.title: This startup is issuing AI-generated acne prescriptions
items.summary: Utah startup Nolla Health lets an AI system analyse face scans and autonomously write acne prescriptions, a notable step for unsupervised AI in medicine.

items.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
items.summary: The Verge reviews a year of AI labs claiming breakthroughs on long-standing maths problems, including a reported Millennium Prize problem, and the controversy around them.

items.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
items.summary: Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19B-parameter omni-model that handles text, images, video and robot control in one network, trained on 320 H100s in about three months.

items.title: Zammad Zero-Day Chain Lets AI Agent Hijack Sessions, Execute Code and Escalate to Root
items.summary: A zero-day chain in the Zammad helpdesk platform allowing session hijacking, code execution and root escalation is reported in connection with an AI agent, adding to autonomous vulnerability-discovery cases.

items.title: China’s AI Safety Money Problem
items.summary: ChinaTalk examines funding shortfalls in China's AI safety research ecosystem.

items.title: Another Historic Cipher Falls to AI
items.summary: Bruce Schneier notes AI has cracked another historic cipher, this one from 1809 written by Napoleon's nephew.

items.title: Building advertising for the way people use AI
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a new visual ad format in ChatGPT, shown during image generation, and expanded measurement, attribution partnerships and brand-suitability controls for advertisers.
